Hydrofluoric acid (HF) is well known for its ability to dissolve glass and other silicon-containing materials. It reacts with silicon dioxide (SiO₂), the main component of glass, to form silicon tetrafluoride (SiF₄) and water. This property makes it particularly useful for etching glass in various applications including the production of frosted glass, laboratory glassware calibration, and in the semiconductor industry.

While hydrofluoric acid has other uses such as in metal cleaning, rust removal, and in the production of fluorine-containing compounds, its most distinctive and well-known application is glass etching.
